doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Monk, Ellington and Archie Shepp in the 1970s
title: Brooklyn, drinking, A.A. and the Amherst workshop
summary: Ware drinks heavily; Gloria suggests A.A., and he plays workshops and a college date with Billy Higgins.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Then I moved up to Brooklyn, moved out to the house that Billy Higgins, drummer, was living in. Gloria and I took a ground-floor apartment and moved the furniture from Philly over there -- piano and everything. But by then, I was drinking this vodka like it was going out of style and Gloria started seeing what it was doing to me and suggested, 'Let's get into A.A.' She join Al-Anon. Tried that and tried it. I failed. Kept trying. During this period, Blackwell called me up. He had a job for me up at Amherst. It was beautiful. You know, they had something like a weekend semin-

ar, workshop. He had Nathan Davis, Dr. Nathan Davis, from the University of Pittsburgh on tenor. We had Clifford Clifton Thornton -- well, Clifford played some kind of East Indian instrument. Bill Cole was the major voice in giving this.

Organizing it. There was Vishnu Wood, Bill Wood on bass -- two basses, Eddie Blackwell and the three horns. I played -- just had one little concert, got my money, come on back to Brooklyn. The next job I had was down here at community college, Billy Higgins and I brought a group down. Played for the students through the help of Gloria and the Black Students League. Dee Dee Bridgewater was supposed to make it with us, but she had a prior engagement. So we brought Roland Alexander, Riane Kenny Zawadi and --
